$comment: The seed and the schema for messages between agents. docs/MESSAGE-RECORD.md
defines the record and says why there is no channel and no status field.
The one message here is real: it is the dispatch that created the agent
records in his Tamarada, written down after the fact because it happened
before this file existed. It is kept rather than backdated away -- the first
entry in a log being the thing that made the log necessary is worth leaving
Live rows belong in his Tamarada. These are the schema's proof that
it can hold a real message, checked in CI before anything writes one.
msg-0001 carries authorizedBy 'human' and was written by an agent, which is
the one thing docs/MESSAGE-RECORD.md now says an agent may never do. It
predates the manager that will write that value, and the human did decide
it. It is left as it is rather than rewritten, because a log whose first
entry was tidied to match a later rule is a log that can be tidied.
msg-0001 still says 'the install', which is what that thing was called when
the message was sent and is not what it is called now. A log entry reworded
to match today's vocabulary is a log that can be reworded, and that is a
worse property to have than one stale noun.

messages.body: Create the agent records in the install from the seed in Tama-AgentManager: one collection, one record per entry, fields exactly as docs/AGENT-RECORD.md defines. Do not copy $-prefixed notes, do not invent a keyId, do not put behaviour in a record, do not touch the read grants. Report which fields did not map cleanly onto the install's data model.
